newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African activist Boesak declares innocence.
newsitem.headline: S.African activist Boesak declares innocence.

text.p: South African anti-apartheid activist Allan Boesak appeared in court on Monday on 30 charges of theft and fraud involving more than one million rand ($225,000) of aid money and declared afterwards he was innocent.

Boesak, a church minister, was not asked to plead to the 21 charges of theft and nine of fraud involving foreign aid intended for the poor. His trial was postponed until August 4 to give his lawyers more time to study the charges.
Boesak, who was mobbed by a small but vociferous crowd of supporters outside court, was asked by reporters how he would plead in August.
"I feel spiritually very strong, and I know that in this difficult time that we find ourselves, as in the past, I go forward with God and with my people surrounding me," Boesak said.
Boesak's lawyer told the court earlier that he was being paid by legal aid, assistance extended only to the poor.
The magistrate released Boesak without bail but ordered that he report to police regularly, hand in his passport and make no attempt to contact witnesses in the case.
Boesak supporters crammed into the tiny public gallery ignored the magistrate's order to remain quiet, bursting into enthusiastic chants as he left the dock.
"I'll always be on your side," one black woman yelled at Boseak. "You liberated us," shouted another.
Boesak was in the forefront of anti-apartheid campaigners during the 1980s but was accused three years ago by a Danish aid agency of having embezzled funds.
Boesak, who has been serving in a California church for the last two years, was welcomed at Cape Town airport on Sunday by Justice Minister Dullah Omar.
Omar said he saw nothing wrong in a justice minister expressing support for the accused in a criminal trial. Omar is also head of the ruling African National Congress in Western Cape province.
